summary.headline: Anthropic previews Claude Duet; malicious LiteLLM release hits PyPI
summary.body: Anthropic previewed Claude Duet, a proactive agent that watches connected apps and works on its own, lifting AI Autonomy by 0.21. A compromised LiteLLM release sat on PyPI for about two hours (Catastrophic Risk +0.30), while OpenAI and PHP maintainers patched critical flaws its model had found (Catastrophic Risk -0.21). Goldman Sachs estimated AI could displace up to 9% of US workers during the transition (Shared Prosperity -0.14). Conquerors and Zookeeper rose and Egalitarian Utopia fell. Successors stayed the leading family. Horizon Balance fell to -15.35 from -15.27.
summary.movers_note: Egalitarian Utopia -0.1, from the LiteLLM compromise (-0.12) and the Goldman forecast (-0.10), partly offset by the PHP patches (+0.08). Conquerors +0.1, from Claude Duet (+0.10) and the LiteLLM compromise (+0.09). Zookeeper +0.1, from Claude Duet (+0.13).

events.title: Anthropic previews Claude Duet, a proactive agent that works across apps
events.summary: Claude Duet, powered by Opus 5.5, monitors connected apps, prioritises tasks and works on its own, asking approval before certain actions. It is a research preview for US Pro/Max users via a waitlist.
events.reason: Moves consumer agents toward acting unprompted; it is a waitlisted preview with approval gates, so T1.

events.title: OpenAI and PHP maintainers patch critical flaws found by an OpenAI model
events.summary: OpenAI worked with PHP maintainers and security partners to patch critical vulnerabilities its GPT Sol model found (Wiz found them separately). It released a checker and proposed a framework for disclosing AI-discovered flaws.
events.reason: AI vulnerability discovery used for coordinated defence of widely used software; self-reported, so T1.

events.title: Malicious LiteLLM v1.107.0 published to PyPI, live for about 2 hours
events.summary: LiteLLM said its v1.107.0 release on PyPI was compromised on Oct 21 and removed after about 2 hours.
events.reason: A confirmed supply-chain attack on a widely used AI library; short-lived with no known impact, so T1.

events.title: Goldman Sachs: AI could displace up to 9% of US workers during the transition
events.summary: Goldman economist Joseph Briggs estimates up to 9% of workers could be displaced if AI lifts productivity by 15%, plus about 3% from slower hiring. Only 23% of US establishments have built AI into workflows.
events.reason: A prominent bank forecast of job displacement; a projection, not an event, so T1 signal.
